Run focused locked/offline Rust tests, canonical-spine/semantic/rejection gates, and final hash guards; the 16 MiB transport rejection alone is not acceptance.

No change to accepted `.axi` bytes, canonical IDs, opaque receipts, or promotion authority.

units.title: General canonical occurrence source map
units.objective: Extend parser-owned, nonserialized source mapping from role carriers to all supported canonical declaration and term occurrences needed by diagnostics and editor services, while proving exact accepted bytes, AST/IR serialization, semantic IDs, and checker input are unchanged.
acceptance: Every supported declaration/term occurrence has an unambiguous typed syntactic address and exact half-open UTF-8 span in the parser's original image.
Source maps remain outside accepted AST, KernelSnapshotIr, digests, certificates, and VerifyMain serialization; removing the map leaves all semantic bytes/IDs identical.
Mapping is linear or otherwise explicitly bounded under existing 4 MiB/line/declaration limits; repeated spellings, comments, multiline syntax, CRLF, and Unicode do not use token-search guessing.
Unsupported/unrecoverable occurrences are represented as absent rather than fabricated coordinates.
validation: Run focused DSL source-map and kernel package/property tests with exact positive/adversarial fixtures.
Run make verify-w02-compiler and compare Rust/Lean corpus outcomes and canonical wire goldens.
Add scale regressions with algorithmic operation bounds; timing may supplement but not establish the bound.
Freeze and review exact changed parser/kernel source before broader compilation.
prerequisites: Use the existing parser and canonical compiler; do not introduce a second recognizer.
Preserve the accepted role-carrier map behavior and monotonic mapping guarantee.

units.title: Versioned relevance corpus and metric kernel
units.objective: Add a public, semantics-free retrieval-evaluation library with versioned query/qrels schemas and exact Recall@k, Precision@k, MRR, and nDCG definitions. Build a non-tiny regression corpus from real versioned Axiograph modules/documents, with hand-reviewed labels, corpus cards, licenses, and no production ranking change.
acceptance: Versioned corpus/query/qrels formats reject unknown versions, duplicate ids, unknown targets, invalid grades, invalid k, and over-limit bytes/items.

The regression corpus contains at least three real Axiograph domain/document packages, at least 500 indexed targets, and at least 100 hand-judged queries; a corpus card records provenance, sampling, assessors, disagreements, and limitations.
Metric definitions explicitly cover no-relevant-result queries, zero returned results, duplicate result ids, deterministic ties, graded relevance, and macro aggregation.
No small-fixture or regression-corpus score is described as production quality.
validation: Run package unit/property tests with hand-calculated rankings for all four metrics, including ties, duplicates, empty rankings, and no-relevant cases.
Run the schema loader against the complete corpus and deliberate malformed fixtures under byte/item limits.
Run native/LSP diagnostics before Cargo checks; run locked offline fmt, Clippy, and tests for the new crate; record exact source/input hashes in the local stage evidence.
Review qrels manually against exact source locators; the reviewer receives frozen corpus, schema, helper, and dependency text plus the complete incremental diff.

No external credentials or live model calls are required.
Do not alter the production retriever in this unit; this establishes metric and data prerequisites for the baseline.

Exact UTF-8 bytes, not normalized text or Rust serialization, remain the revision anchor; comments, whitespace, and order stay identity-significant.
Rust and Lean independently reconstruct their ASTs; the contract does not permit deserializing Rust IR as Lean source meaning.
Resource bounds and stable rejection classes are stated as operational contracts, not theorems.

Run `make verify-axi-parse-e2e` and `make verify-identity-parity`.
Run `python3 scripts/check_book.py` and local link checks; no broad checklist closure.

Reuse the pinned environment under `build/engineering-quality/release-roadmap/complete-kani-with-verified-path-20260908T044738Z`; do not reconstruct PATH.
Review any changed trust-language and exact-byte framing before dependent units.

units.objective: Validate every live frontend JSON ingress with production validators and deterministic resource bounds while leaving opaque receipt/checker metadata non-authoritative.

Run pinned frontend gates and focused `db_server_e2e`; disclose browser coverage separately.

Use fresh temporary stores only and production AxiStore APIs.
If graph/query highlighting requires a new authority binding, escalate the trust-boundary design before implementation.

units.title: Bounded multi-diagnostic taxonomy and conservative suggestions
units.objective: Introduce a typed diagnostic collector that reports multiple independent parse/import/type errors with generalized locations and conservative namespace-aware suggestions, while preserving deterministic order and explicit unlocated fallbacks.
acceptance: Collector has explicit item/count/byte/work bounds and deterministic source order; one malformed declaration cannot make unrelated locations guess or drift.
Typed subjects become checked refs only after successful resolution; parse/import/missing-file errors use truthful syntactic or unlocated subjects.
Suggestions are unique, namespace-correct, bounded, advisory, and absent for ties/unsupported namespaces/stale images.
Overall validation and promotion stay failed when multiple errors are paged or hidden.

Run focused authoring diagnostic/full/compact tests and source_diagnostics_cli.
Rerun make verify-w02-compiler and compact page-union/identity tests.
Review diagnostic ordering and resource complexity against SECURITY_BOUNDARIES.md.

Choose recovery/accumulation points that do not change which canonical-invalid inputs are rejected or make invalid modules executable.

units.title: Production-path retrieval baseline and ablation report
units.objective: Expose the released retrieval algorithm through a reusable library-owned service without changing ranking semantics, prove adapter parity, and run the EQ-10 corpus through the actual service with lexical/token-hash, precomputed-model-vector, graph-enrichment, and hybrid ablations. Freeze the baseline before replacement work.
acceptance: The evaluation command directly calls the same public service used by production CLI/grounding adapters; it does not copy ranking logic, include private source, or execute the CLI.
Refactor-only parity fixtures freeze released rankings, component scores, ties, limits, truncation, and errors before any algorithm replacement.

A bounded report records source state, corpus/qrels digest, accepted snapshot/materialization where applicable, retriever/method version, index and model identities, dimensions, normalization, query limits, per-query result counts, omissions, metrics, operation counts, and measured latency.
Precomputed query/target vectors carry public model/version-or-digest and text identities, so vector ablations run offline without provider credentials.
Ranking/metric content is deterministic; wall-clock observations are explicitly non-deterministic measurements and excluded from the report content digest.
validation: Run the deterministic offline command twice and compare all content except explicitly labeled timing observations.
Run production adapter parity tests and deliberate stale snapshot, wrong model/dimension, malformed vector, duplicate result, tie, zero-overlap, and limit cases.
Run lexical-only, vector-only, graph-only, lexical+graph, and full-hybrid ablations over the complete RG-U01 corpus; record baseline before RG-U04 or later ranking edits.
Run locked offline package/workspace-scoped tests, Clippy, fmt, and the relevant canonical/regulated-shipment grounding workflow without live providers or accepted-store mutation.
prerequisites: RG-U01 corpus and metrics are frozen and reviewed.
Precomputed embedding artifacts must have documented public model identity/license and exact digests; do not call a live provider.
The change is refactor/instrumentation only until the baseline artifact exists and parity is independently reviewed.

units.title: Deterministic Rust/Lean differential parser runner
units.objective: Replace small acceptance-only comparisons with bounded normalized-AST, digest, typecheck, and rejection-class differential evidence driven by the shared contract.
acceptance: A deterministic seed records generator version, seed, case count, maximum bytes/depth/counts, and stable ordering.
Both binaries emit a contract-defined normalized AST/rejection envelope; the runner compares parse, digest, typecheck/formation, and rejection class, not only exit status.
Hand-calculated positive and negative goldens catch shared-bug agreement and unsupported-as-success behavior.
Runner fails on timeout, truncation, malformed output, zero cases, duplicate case IDs, or an unrecognized rejection class.

Run `make verify-w02-compiler`, `make verify-axi-parse-e2e`, and `make verify-identity-parity`.
Run actual Rust and Lean binaries on at least one hand-audited case from every contract section.

Exact Rust 1.98 and checked-in Lean toolchain available through the preserved environment.
No generated case may alter existing accepted `.axi` examples; use new fixtures or temporary inputs.
Compiler/helper invocations must stay within the stated 600-second subprocess bound and explicit output limits.

units.objective: Make current documentation consistently distinguish design targets, historical baselines, runtime checks, operational release evidence, and trusted formal results without converting bounded slices into broad completion.

The 70c568b audit and append-only historical validation records remain identifiable as historical evidence.

Do not edit historical audit observations except to add clearly dated correction notes outside quoted baseline text.

Rich sections, navigation, list/detail/draft/status behavior, and evidence-only controls retain functionality.

Review source-map use against exact accepted bytes and confirm no semantic identity changes.

New unsaved roots and unsaved imported modules compile as one exact overlay closure without writing disk or mixing stale disk bytes.

Production CLI and accepted/evidence grounding adapters use the shared lexical ranker, not duplicated or test-only logic.

Unknown limits, oversized text/corpora, stale indexes, and unsupported tokenization configurations fail closed or report explicit bounded truncation.

Run RG-U02 adapter parity where semantics should remain invariant and record intentional ranking deltas separately.
Run RG-U01 metrics against the frozen baseline and report quality and latency regressions without claiming production quality.
Run locked offline dependency, test, Clippy, fmt, security, and relevant grounding/regulated-shipment checks; reject unrelated lockfile churn.

Official docs and the selected crate version must be available for review; if discovery fails, preserve the exact error and stop this unit without source mutation.
No external credentials are required.

units.objective: Mechanically align pure contract vocabulary and remove safe duplicate interpretation paths while preserving independent trusted reconstruction.
acceptance: Mechanical drift check covers AST tags, role/refinement/constraint/rewrite kinds, relevant bounds, and rejection codes.
Ad hoc alternate parser or canonical-meaning helpers are removed only where the contract and differential corpus prove equivalent behavior.
Lean continues to parse exact source and independently reconstruct category/type meaning; no Rust AST/IR deserializer enters `VerifyMain`.
Any deliberately duplicated semantic implementation is documented as an independence requirement rather than falsely counted as removed.

Review complete release-to-current and incremental new-file-aware diffs; run `cargo fmt --check` only before the final hash-guarded validation.

CLI, predictive-proposal, and test callers use the public API; no private source inclusion or process facade remains.
OpenAI, Anthropic, and Ollama retain their distinct authentication, endpoint, peer-pinning, timeout, and response rules.

Run all nine strict feature configurations plus `feature_boundaries_cli` in all supported configurations.
Run full locked workspace tests and focused predictive/LLM/security tests on final bytes; record source/dependency rationale and lockfile review.

Choose whether the public owner is an existing crate or a narrowly justified new crate from dependency analysis; do not overload `axiograph-llm-sync` merely for naming convenience.
Preserve evidence-plane output and fail-closed promotion boundaries.

acceptance: Syntax types parse without PathDB execution or verifier dependencies; elaboration consumes explicit compiled/runtime schema context.

Unsupported identity collisions continue to reject before DB construction; local-name behavior is not broadened silently.
CLI, MCP, LSP, HTTP, CQ, and external clients consume the same public elaboration API.
validation: Run parser/property/golden tests plus import-aware, namespace-collision, typed-hole, refinement, CRLF/Unicode, and malformed query cases.
Compare library and CLI prepared-query metadata and trust outputs for canonical/import-aware fixtures.
Run required non-vacuous prepared-query selectors, canonical spine, full locked workspace tests, strict query/CLI Clippy, and formatting.

Coordinate with the broader EQ04 qualified-resolution requirement; this unit must not claim to implement it accidentally.

units.objective: Create a public library owner for complete workspace authoring requests, reports, import resolution, compact projection, validation, CQ/query orchestration, olog repair, evolution preview, and promotion review, leaving the CLI as an adapter.
acceptance: A public crate exposes explicit typed request/options/report/service surfaces for the complete current workspace behavior.
The crate has no CLI, MCP, HTTP, LSP, REPL, LLM, or editor dependency and owns moved implementation rather than including private source.

Run workspace format/strict Clippy/tests plus canonical-spine, semantics, regulated-shipment, and required query selection guards.

Review `docs/reference/SOFTWARE_AUTHORING_TOOLS.md`, `KERNEL_IR.md`, `RUST_LIFECYCLE_TYPES.md`, `SECURITY_BOUNDARIES.md`, and `RUST_ARCHITECTURE_CLEANUP.md`.
One writer; no broad crate move without a frozen complete source/dependency/caller review package.

units.title: Typed hybrid rank fusion and request-scoped embedding reuse
units.objective: Replace max fusion with one named tested fusion policy, make component scores provider-neutral, record the exact retrieval method, and compute one query embedding per complete shared model identity within a request.
acceptance: The report exposes typed components such as lexical_score, vector_score, graph_score, component rank, fusion score, and method/version; it removes the false Ollama-specific meaning from provider-neutral results.
Fusion is rank-based or calibrated under a documented finite policy and cannot compare raw incomparable scales with max.

One request-scoped query embedding is reused only when backend, model, version/digest/deployment, dimension, normalization, and prompt/text policy all match; mismatches trigger separate computation or fail closed.
Tie order, top-k bounds, snapshot scope, omissions, and evidence-only authority are stable and explicit.
No compatibility alias is retained unless an explicit accepted wire contract requires it.
validation: Use counting fake provider boundaries around the real production service to prove one call for shared entity/chunk model identity and separate calls for mismatches; no test-only ranker replaces production behavior.
Exercise mixed score scales, absent components, duplicate ids, ties, NaN/infinity rejection, zero overlap, and deterministic repeated runs.
Run lexical/vector/graph/hybrid ablations and compare against RG-U02 and RG-U04 results.
Run feature-matrix compile/tests for enabled and disabled providers without live requests, plus locked fmt/Clippy/tests.
prerequisites: RG-U04 shared lexical service is reviewed.
RG-U02 baseline identities and report schema are frozen.
No live provider call is allowed; provider behavior tests use bounded local fakes at the existing network boundary.

units.title: Dependent retyping for category-kernel wire paths
units.objective: Convert validated index-based category and formal-groupoid paths into dependent Lean paths over the exact reconstructed presentation.
acceptance: Forward and signed wire paths retype only when every index, direction, and endpoint composes over the exact presentation.
Success yields `Path p a b` or `GroupoidPath p a b` with endpoints in the type; invalid endpoint/index/composition cases reject.
Round-trip/erasure lemmas show retyped paths retain the exact wire word and endpoints.
No theorem interprets a formal inverse as an executable inverse of ontology data.
validation: Build and run focused Lean tests for empty identities, forward generators, inverse generators, mixed words, and N/N+1 invalid indexes.
Run `make verify-lean-e2e-category-kernel-v3` and `make verify-lean-theory`.
Run the first-party no-`axiom`/no-`sorry`/no-`unsafe def` scan used by `verify-lean-theory`.
prerequisites: EQ16-U01 fixes the wire/AST contract.
Use current mathlib/Lean lockfiles; no `lake update` or new axiom.
Formal reviewer checks dependent casts and endpoint equalities, not only executable test results.

units.title: Extract LLM tool execution and retrieval services
units.objective: Move tool-loop execution and current retrieval/ranking behavior behind bounded public services after provider contracts stabilize, deduplicating entity/chunk processing without changing ranking semantics prematurely.
acceptance: Tool execution has explicit typed inputs, resource limits, and output/trust contracts independent of provider transport.
Entity and chunk ranking share only genuinely identical typed mechanics; token and embedding scores remain distinguishable and deterministic.
The production retrieval baseline is preserved before EQ10/EQ11 changes; no exhaustive scan is renamed ANN and no exact fallback is hidden.
Model outputs, retrieved evidence, and scores cannot mint accepted state or certificates.
validation: Golden/parity tests compare pre-extraction and post-extraction production outputs for deterministic fixtures, ties, duplicate IDs, empty results, stale snapshots, and mixed score availability.
Run real process-free library consumers and CLI/REPL parity without invoking live providers.
Rerun compact client parity, full locked workspace tests, strict feature matrix, security tests, and retrieval bounds on final bytes.
prerequisites: Capture a production-path retrieval baseline before changing code shape.
Do not select BM25, fusion, ANN, or reranking behavior in this architecture-only unit; those depend on EQ10 evaluation.

units.title: Separate query execution and certification lifecycle
units.objective: Give finite execution and certificate policy distinct public modules joined by one typed prepared-query handle, preserving opaque verified receipts and checker approval requirements.
acceptance: Execution requires a prepared handle bound to the same DB/snapshot identity; certification consumes exact source/query/answer/certificate identities.
Verified receipt types remain output-only and cannot be created by Deserialize, Default, unchecked constructors, or report metadata.
HTTP read-only query execution does not imply checker readiness or certificate authority.
All adapters share one certificate-policy implementation and retain explicit unsupported/non-claim states.
validation: Run same-DB/cross-DB, source/query/answer/certificate tamper, stale handle, disabled checker, malformed receipt, and compile-fail construction tests.
Run all required guarded query tests after Lean checker prerequisites, `verify-canonical-spine`, `verify-semantics`, and regulated-shipment exact-query rejection.
Run external process-free client and CLI/REPL/server parity plus full workspace tests and strict feature matrix.

Do not change certificate versions or trusted import closure as a refactor side effect.

Canonical and import-aware fixtures retain exact source closure, query/CQ/trust results, and stable identities equivalent to CLI output.

Example output clearly separates runtime evidence, emitted certificate metadata, verified receipt state, and accepted promotion.

Compare its reports to actual CLI/adapters on software-authoring and regulated-shipment fixtures.
Exercise malformed paths, changed unsaved buffers/imports, unsupported projection namespaces, missing CQ/checker receipt, and resource bounds.
Run locked/offline package tests and canonical/semantic/rejection gates.

Use exact canonical sources and temporary workspaces; no accepted-store mutation is needed.

Run the real semantic-search and accepted-grounding workflows and verify no automatic proposal, commit, promotion, or accepted-store mutation occurs.
Record native/LSP diagnostics before final hash-guarded validation; freeze logs, dependencies, helpers, complete incremental diff, and release-to-current new-file-aware diff.

Use the prepared exact tool environment and bounded subprocess helper; a 600-second command bound is not permission for an unbounded suite.
Do not mark roadmap completion or commit without parent acceptance.
